image.alt: A Philodendron White Princess in a white pot, its dark leaves splashed with white and cream on pink-red stems

light.label: Bright indirect light
light.note: Tolerates medium light, but the white fades and new leaves come back greener

landscape_use.note: Frost-free zones, never in direct sun

snap: A compact, upright Philodendron with dark leaves splashed in white and cream, held on striking pink-red stems. No two leaves are marked the same. It needs bright, filtered light to keep the white, and is toxic to cats and dogs if chewed.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: A cultivated form of Philodendron erubescens, a climbing aroid from the rainforests of South America. It stays compact and upright for a long while, then slowly begins to climb and will happily take a small moss pole.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Water when the top inch of the mix has dried, using a loose, airy aroid mix that drains fast — these roots rot quickly in heavy soil. Bright filtered light is what keeps the white coming; in a dim corner the new leaves revert to plain green.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: The variegation is unstable, so every leaf is a surprise: clean white patches, fine speckling, or a half-and-half split down the middle. The pink-red stems are what tell a true White Princess apart from a White Knight or a White Wizard.
